content: 1. In patients with transient or persistent reduction in urinary output due to renal insufficiency, the total daily dose of cefpodoxime proxetil should be reduced. This is because usual doses can lead to high and prolonged serum antibiotic concentrations in such individuals. 2. Cefpodoxime, like other cephalosporins, should be used cautiously in patients receiving concurrent treatment with potent diuretics. 3. Prolonged use of cefpodoxime proxetil may result in the overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms. Regular evaluation of the patient’s condition is essential, and if superinfection occurs during therapy, appropriate measures should be taken. 4. Prescribing cefpodoxime proxetil (VANTIN) in the absence of a proven or strongly suspected bacterial infection or a prophylactic indication is unlikely to benefit the patient and increases the risk of developing drug-resistant bacteria. 5. Patients should be informed that antibacterial drugs, including VANTIN, should only be used to treat bacterial infections and not viral infections (e.g., the common cold). 6. When VANTIN is prescribed for a bacterial infection, patients should be advised to take the medication exactly as directed, even if they feel better early in the course of therapy. Skipping doses or not completing the full course of therapy may reduce the effectiveness of the treatment and increase the likelihood of bacteria developing resistance, making them untreatable by VANTIN or other antibacterial drugs in the future. 7. Diarrhea is a common side effect of antibiotics and usually resolves when the antibiotic is discontinued. However, patients may develop watery and bloody stools (with or without stomach cramps and fever) even as late as two or more months after completing the antibiotic course. If this occurs, they should contact their physician immediately. 8. Concomitant administration of high doses of antacids (e.g., sodium bicarbonate and aluminum hydroxide) or H2 blockers reduces peak plasma levels of cefpodoxime by 24% to 42% and the extent of absorption by 27% to 32%. However, the rate of absorption is not affected. 9. Concomitant administration of drugs like propantheline delays peak plasma levels of cefpodoxime (47% increase in Tmax) but does not affect the extent of absorption (AUC). 10. Probenecid inhibits the renal excretion of cefpodoxime, leading to an approximately 31% increase in AUC and a 20% increase in peak plasma levels of cefpodoxime. 11. Although nephrotoxicity has not been observed when cefpodoxime proxetil is administered alone, close monitoring of renal function is recommended when it is used concomitantly with compounds known to have nephrotoxic potential. 12. Cephalosporins, including cefpodoxime proxetil, are known to occasionally induce a positive direct Coombs' test. 13. Long-term animal studies to evaluate the carcinogenic potential of cefpodoxime proxetil have not been conducted. Mutagenesis studies, including the Ames test, chromosome aberration test, unscheduled DNA synthesis assay, mitotic recombination and gene conversion, forward gene mutation assay, and in vivo micronucleus test, were all negative. 14. No adverse effects on fertility or reproduction were observed in rats when cefpodoxime proxetil was administered orally at doses up to 100 mg/kg/day (2 times the human dose based on mg/m²). 15. Cefpodoxime proxetil is classified as Pregnancy Category B. It was neither teratogenic nor embryocidal when administered to rats during organogenesis at doses up to 100 mg/kg/day (2 times the human dose based on mg/m²) or to rabbits at doses up to 30 mg/kg/day (1–2 times the human dose based on mg/m²). However, there are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. This drug should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed. 16. Cefpodoxime proxetil has not been studied for use during labor and delivery. Treatment should only be given if clearly necessary. 17. Cefpodoxime is excreted in human milk. In a study of three lactating women, cefpodoxime levels in human milk were 0%, 2%, and 6% of concomitant serum levels at 4 hours after a 200 mg oral dose. At 6 hours post-dosing, levels were 0%, 9%, and 16% of concomitant serum levels. Due to the potential for serious reactions in nursing infants, a decision should be made to discontinue nursing or discontinue the drug, considering the importance of the drug to the mother. 18. The safety and efficacy of cefpodoxime proxetil in infants less than 2 months of age have not been established. 19. Of the 3,338 patients in multiple-dose clinical studies of cefpodoxime proxetil film-coated tablets, 521 (16%) were aged 65 and over, while 214 (6%) were aged 75 and over. No overall differences in effectiveness or safety were observed between elderly and younger patients. Pharmacokinetic parameters were unchanged relative to those observed in healthy younger subjects. Dose adjustment in elderly patients with normal renal function is not necessary.
